subject: Trouble with RW2 model on linear coefficients

messages.author: f1572a038d61492c
messages.subject: Trouble with RW2 model on linear coefficients
parts:
Hi,

I know not having a reproducible example is bad form, but my data is not shareable and I'm not entirely sure how to reproduce the bug.

I have longitudinal data of cortisol and testosterone measures for individuals going through puberty. Letting a represent age bin (a = 1 corresponds to [8, 8.5), a = 2  is [8.5, 9), etc..), I want to fit the following model:

test_{ai} | \eta_{ai}, \tau_y, \tau_{beta} \tau_{gamma} ~ N(\eta_{ai}, \tau_y^{-1})
\eta_{ia} = \alpha_a + \beta_a x cort_{ai} + \gamma_i
\beta_a ~ RW2(\tau_{beta})
\gamma_i ~ N(0, \tau_{gamma}^{-1})

Where test_{ai} are log testosterone observations and cort_{ai} are log cortisol observations for individual i at age group a, \alpha_a are age bin-specific intercepts, \gamma_i are IID random intercepts for each individual, and \beta_a are coefficients describing the linear relationship between cortisol and testosterone for those in age bin a with a smoothing prior on them. 

To specify this model I use the following formula and inla() call

formula_HC <- testosterone_log ~ -1 + age_binyrhalf +
f(fieldcode,  model = "iid") +
f(age_binyr_idx, values = cortisol_log, model = "rw2", scale.model = TRUE)

mod_HC <- inla(formula_HC, data = mod_data, family = "gaussian")

where age_binyrhalf is a factor variable with my age groups, field code is a character variable with unique individual identifiers, and age_binyr_idx is a numeric vector with values 1, 2, etc. corresponding to the numeric levels associated with the categorial labels of age_binyrhalf. 

The issue is when I try to run this, I get an error that The 'values' given in f(age_binyr_idx, ..., values=) are not unique, it tells me I have 440 unique values instead of 446. (Attaching a screenshot of the output). However, tests of equality/tables, etc of my values show I have 446 unique values. I suspect this is maybe due to some rounding issues within INLA.

Can anyone help me with this issue? 

Thank you! And, sorry again, that I cannot reproduce this issue with simulated data (I tried!)

All the best,
Jessica Godwin

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Trouble with RW2 model on linear coefficients
parts:
Hi J,

I think the name 'values' is causing the confusion, as 'values' defined where
the RW2 is defined, while the 'weights', ie your covariate values, goes into the
2nd unnamed argument.

I would try with


f(age_binyr_idx, cortisol_log, model = "rw2", constr=FALSE, scale.model = TRUE)

normally, constr=F is required as you do not want the coefficients to sum to
zero

let me know

H
